text:
jamie: Heads-up — after the 02:00 driver/firmware rollout in us-west-2 we observed a ~3x uptick in Xid PCIe errors and a handful of nodes hitting ECC corrections. Not catastrophic but noisy. Anyone else seeing patterns?

sasha: I see the same trend in telemetry. Xid spikes clustered around GPUs on p4d-ssd pools, mostly during long-running batch inferences.

prasad: Can you paste the query you used? I'll correlate with kernel logs and pod drain history.

jamie: Query I ran quickly: ```sql
-- counts by gpu_model and xid_type last 6h
SELECT gpu_model, xid_type, count(*) FROM metrics.gpu_events
WHERE ts > now() - interval '6 hours' GROUP BY 1,2 ORDER BY 3 DESC;
```

alex: Quick note: the rollout included a minor kernel module change + new firmware blob (nvfw v2.4.1). Might be a timing regression on ECC reporting path.

infra-bot: [deploy-bot] rollout/driver-2026-03-18 completed to us-west-2 (23 hosts). See: https://ci.internal/rollouts/driver-2026-03-18

prasad: I pulled syslogs from two noisy hosts: attached snippet: ```
Mar 18 02:12:03 host-gpu-12 kernel: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, GPU has fallen off the bus.
Mar 18 02:12:03 host-gpu-12 kernel: pcieport 0000:64:00.0: AER: Corrected error received: id 00e0
Mar 18 02:12:04 host-gpu-12 nvidia-mig: ecc corrected: 1428
```

jamie: Thanks. I also see higher latency for long seq model runs right before Xid. Could be thermal or sustained power draw interaction.

sasha: Proposed triage plan: 1) roll back the kernel module on 3 non-prod hosts and run a 6-hour stress job; 2) run focused nvml stress + heat soak on a noisy host with old vs new firmware; 3) increase ECC telemetry sampling (10s -> 1s) for 1h to catch pre-Xid hints. Thoughts? :mag:

alex: +1 to the plan. Add a check for recent PCIe link retrain in dmesg, and capture PCIe counters with `lspci -vvv` before/after.

prasad: I'll schedule the rollback on two canary hosts (gpu-canary-a/b) now, and kick off nvml stress. Tagging @oncall-bot for paging rules if Xid > 10 in 10m on prod pools.

oncall-bot: [alert-config] updated: page oncall if Xid_count(product_pools, 10m) >= 10.

jamie: For gate criteria: if rollback reduces Xid rate by >=50% on canaries during a 3h window we hold the rollout and auto-open a backout. If no change, escalate to HW vendor. Agree?

alex: Agreed. Also capture GPU power draw from smi and host BMC temps. If power draw spikes precede Xid, we may need firmware/hardware patch.

prasad: Rolling now. I'll paste results in ~3h. In the meantime, leaving traffic steering rules to divert long-run jobs off potentially flaky nodes (kube taint + pod disruption).

jamie: Thanks. If anybody sees a new fleet-wide pattern (other regions) call it out. I'll prepare a short postmortem template we can fill if we end up gating the rollout. :memo:

sasha: one more datapoint — us-east-1 shows no uptick. Suggests it's specific to the us-west-2 hardware/firmware combo.

prasad: update 30m: after rollback on gpu-canary-a we ran a 90m stress and Xid count went from 8->1 in the window. Capturing full logs now. Looks promising.

jamie: Nice. Hold the rest of the rollout pending a 3h confirmation. I'll update the rollout ticket.

infra-bot: [rollout] driver-2026-03-18 paused for us-west-2 based on manual hold by jamie.

oncall-bot: [incident-note] created INCIDENT-2026-0318-02: Xid spike after driver/firmware rollout, investigating.

alex: OK moving to collect vendor debug: please grab `nvidia-bug-report.sh` output and attach to the incident. Also include `dmidecode` and `bmc` power logs.

jamie: Will collect and add. Thanks team — quick, clean process so far. Keep updates here. :thumbsup:
